sentences.text:
An Application Under Section 401/482 Of ... vs M/S. Krishna
Traders & Ors on 28 August, 2019

Author: Tirthankar Ghosh
Bench: Tirthankar Ghosh
Sl. August C.R.R. 2522 of 2004
79. 28, 2019 In the matter of: An application under Section 401/482 of the Code of Criminal
Procedure;
And In the matter of : M/s. Krishna Traders & ors.
Versus State of West Bengal & anr.
No one appears in support of the revision petition, when the matter is taken up for consideration.
No accommodation is also sought for.

I find from the records of the case that the subject matter of challenge in this revisional application is related to judgment and order dated March 11, 2004 passed by the learned Sessions Judge, Third Bench, City Sessions Court at Calcutta, in Criminal Appeal No. 9 of 2000 whereby the appellate court was pleased to affirm the judgment and order dated December 28, 1999 passed by the learned Municipal Magistrate, Third Court at Calcutta, in Case No. 47D of 1988 under Section 16(1)(a)(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.

entities.text: Sessions Judge, Third Bench, City Sessions Court at Calcutta
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: It is, however, seen that after an order of suspension of sentence and stay of realisation of fine was passed on December 14, 2009 by a co-ordinate bench of this court, the petitioners are not seriously pursuing the revisional application.
Under such circumstances, the revisional application bearing C.R.R. 2522 of 2004 is dismissed for default.
The learned Municipal Magistrate, Third Court at Calcutta, is directed to execute the sentence passed in connection with Case No. 47D of 1988.

entities.text: Municipal Magistrate, Third Court at Calcutta
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Office is directed to communicate this order to the court below.

opennyai_summary.decision:
No accommodation is also sought for.
It is, however, seen that after an order of suspension of sentence and stay of realisation of fine was passed on December 14, 2009 by a co-ordinate bench of this court, the petitioners are not seriously pursuing the revisional application.
Under such circumstances, the revisional application bearing C.R.R. 2522 of 2004 is dismissed for default.
The learned Municipal Magistrate, Third Court at Calcutta, is directed to execute the sentence passed in connection with Case No. 47D of 1988.
